# Dmitry Solovyev

## Statistician | Data Scientist | Policy Analyst 

### About me

Hi there! If you landed (somehow) on this page, it means you'd like to know more about who I am.

My name is Dmitry, and I'm a data scientist with a background in public policy and statistics.

Right now, I work at TriMet, the public transit agency in Portland, Oregon, where I develop predictive models, design interactive dashboards, and support teams across planning, engineering, and customer experience. My work focuses on making sense of ridership patterns, testing service changes, and helping stakeholders understand what the data is really saying. I primarily use R and Python for my analysis and try to make sure that everyone could understand the results of my work no matter their background.

Originally from Russia, I have quite a diverse career path. Before TriMet, I spent nearly four years at Oregon State University. There, I completed two master’s degrees: one in Public Policy and another in Statistics, with an emphasis on biostatistics and experimental design. I also worked as a statistical consultant and teaching assistant, helping public health researchers design studies and analyze results, and teaching students how to approach real-world problems using data (to the best of my abilities).

Before moving to the US, I worked in public policy NGOs, where I built simulation models, evaluated large-scale interventions, and supported strategic decision-making in areas like healthcare, housing, and energy policy. I also obtained degrees in political science and international relations, so rest assured, there are topics to talk about on Friday evening with me.

Please feel free to hit me up with any questions. I'm still think about turning this page into some kind of mini-blog, and, who knows, I might do it one day.

If you are interested, there is also a small list of projects I worked on at some point - you can also go visit my github.
